sentences.text:
Both appeals arising out of the common Judgment and Award dated 03.08.2017 passed in MVC.Nos.699 and 700 of 2016 by the IX Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., Belagavi (for short, 'the Tribunal').
2. The appellant/petitioners have preferred these appeals for enhancement of compensation and also questioning the liability fixed by the Tribunal only to the extent of 50% on the Insurance Company.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Parties herein are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
4. In the present case, the claimants put forth the following essential details in their claim petitions submitted to the Tribunal.
On the date of 9th November 2015, around 07:15 hours, both petitioners were passengers aboard a TATA APE Rickshaw.

During their journey, a Bolero vehicle with registration number MH-09/CM-9623, driven by its designated driver, recklessly and negligently approached from the opposite NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB direction.
This Bolero vehicle collided with their rickshaw, causing both claimants to suffer injuries.
In the aftermath of the accident, they underwent medical treatment, incurring substantial medical expenses.
Additionally, the claimants sustained lasting physical disabilities due to the injuries sustained.
It is alleged that the fault for the incident lies squarely on the driver of the Bolero vehicle.

As a result, respondents 1 and 2, who respectively represent the vehicle's owner and its insurer, are considered liable to provide compensation for the resultant damages and losses experienced by the claimants.

5. In response to the service of notice, both respondents have appeared through their respective counsel and filed their separate objections by denying the contents of petitions and contended that the amount of compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and the alleged accident has occurred due to the fault of the driver of said TATA APE vehicle.
The owner and the insurer of TATA APE vehicle are necessary parties to the petitions.
The petitions suffer from non-joinder of necessary parties.

The 1st respondent further contended that his vehicle was validly insured with respondent No.2 and driver NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB of the vehicle was having valid driving licence as such,
the liability, if any, may be saddled with respondent No.2.
On all these grounds they sought for dismissal of both petitions.

After clubbing of both petitions, the Tribunal, based on the rival pleadings in both claim petitions,
has framed the common issues as under:
"(1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 09.11.2015 at about 07.15 hours within the limits of New Pargaon village near Asmita Daba, petitioner sustained injuries in the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the vehicle bearing registration no.MH-09/CM-9623 by its driver?
(2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
(3) What order?"
7. In order to prove their case, petitioners got examined themselves as PWs.1 and 2 respectively, and also examined the Doctor as PW-3 and got marked 21 documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P-21.
Respondents have not adduced any oral evidence.
Ex.R1-insurance policy is marked as Ex.R1 with consent.

On hearing arguments from both sides, the Tribunal has given the findings to the points as under:
Point No.1: Partly in the affirmative.
Point No.2:

Petitioner in MVC.No.699/2016 and  petitioner in MVC.No.700/2016 are  entitled for compensation of  Rs.2,01,092/- and Rs.2,53,932/-
 respectively from the 2nd  respondent.
Point No.3:
As per final order.

9. In view of the above findings, the Tribunal has allowed both petitions in part by its common Judgment dated 03.08.2017 and awarded compensation of Rs.2,01,092/- to the petitioner in MVC.No.699/2016 and Rs.2,53,932/- to the petitioner in MVC.No.700/2016 with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petitions till their realization.
Out of the compensation amount, the Tribunal has deducted 50% of the compensation on the ground that petitioners have not impleaded the insured and insurer of TATA APE vehicle.

Being aggrieved by the common Judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, petitioners/claimants in both petitions have preferred these appeals for enhancement of compensation and also NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB questioning the deduction of 50% out of the compensation amount.

Learned counsel for appellants filed I.A.No.1/2021 under Order XLI Rule 27 read with Section 151 of Code of Civil Procedure to permit the appellants to produce additional documents i.e., certified copies of charge sheet in Criminal Case No.68/2016 and translated copy of charge sheet, the panchanama dated 09.11.2015 and rough sketch.
Same was allowed by this Court as per the order dated 14.08.2023 and same are received on record.

11. The learned counsel appearing for petitioners has submitted her arguments that the Judgment and Award passed by the Tribunal fixing the liability on the driver of TATA APE vehicle to the extent of 50% is contrary to law, facts, procedure and the material on record.

With regard to the MVC.No.699/2016 is concerned, she submits that the appellant has sustained injuries as shown in the Wound Certificate and Doctor has opined that he has sustained permanent physical disability to the tune of 50% in respect of right lower limb, 35% to the left lower limb and 20% to the right upper limb.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB

However, the Tribunal has erred in not relying upon the evidence of P.W.3 on the ground that he is not a treated Doctor and considering the disability only to the extent of 12% for the purpose of awarding compensation.
The Tribunal ought to have considered the disability of the petitioner at 70%.
Further it is submitted that the Tribunal has not awarded just and proper compensation on all other heads.
On all these grounds, sought for allowing of the appeal.
12. The learned counsel further submits that pertaining to MVC.No.700/2016, the Tribunal has failed to consider the disability certificate Ex.P.12.
The Doctor (P.W.3) has opined that petitioner has permanent physical disability to the extent of 60% to left lower limb and 30% to right lower limb.
However, the Tribunal has erred in not relying the evidence of P.W.3 and has taken the disability at 12%.
The Tribunal ought to have considered the disability of the petitioner at 70%.

The Tribunal has also not awarded the just and proper compensation to the other heads as per the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Santosh Devi vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd and Other, reported in 2012 ACJ 1428.

sentences.text: On all these grounds sought for allowing of this appeal.

As against this, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submit that the Tribunal has passed the impugned Judgment and Award in accordance with law and facts and there are no grounds to interfere with the same, accordingly sought for dismissal of the appeals.

14. Having heard the arguments on both sides, the following points would arise for our consideration :
(1) Whether the Tribunal has committed an error in taking the award amount to the extent of 50% only on the ground that owner and insurer of the TATA APE motor vehicle is not impleaded in the claim petitions?

15. Our answers to the above points are as under :
Point No.1 in the affirmative.
Point No.2 partly in the affirmative.
Point No.3 as per the final order.
16. We have carefully examined the material placed on the record.

The Tribunal in paragraph No.11 has observed as under:
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB "11.
It is to be noted that the petitioners have not produced copy of charge sheet and also the rough sketch of the spot before the court.
In the cross examination, PW 1 has admitted that the police have prepared the rough sketch at the spot.
Moreover, the petitioner Yashawant has not produced his driving license to show that he was having valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle at the time of accident.
Even he has not produced the insurance policy of his vehicle.
In the absence of charge sheet and rough sketch & in view the admission of PW 1, it can safely be said that petitioner Yashawant Laxman Gosavi was also at fault in causing the accident.
So, the contention of learned counsel for respondent no.2 that the petitioner by coming in wrong side dashed to the on coming vehicle, appears to be true and it is trustworthy.

Therefore, it is clear from the evidence of PW 1 & 2 coupled with Ex.P1, 2, 4, & 9 that the accident took place due to the fault on the part of petitioner Yashawant and also the driver of bolero vehicle, as such in my opinion both of them have equally contributed their negligence in causing the accident and it is considered at the ratio of 50% each.

Therefore, I answer issue No.1 partly in the affirmative."
17.

Upon careful examination of the provided evidence, it becomes evident that based on a complaint filed by - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB Bhajarang Dattatraya Powar, Assistant Sub-Inspector of Vadagaon Police Station in the Kolhapur District, a case was registered by the Station House Officer of Vadagaon Police Station under Crime No.241/2015.
This case was registered against Malik Ahmad Mulla, the driver of the Bolero vehicle bearing registration number MH-09/CM-9623.
The charges included offenses under Sections 279, 337, 338, and 427 of the Indian Penal Code, read in conjunction with Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Following the registration of the case, a Shri Sachin S/O Sakharam Gosavi vs Shri. Balavant S/O Baburao Barge on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140503038/
6 thorough investigation was carried out by the Investigating Officer, resulting in the submission of a charge sheet against the Bolero vehicle's driver for the aforementioned offenses.

sentences.text: While the petitioners presented notarized copies of the charge sheet and other relevant documents to the Tribunal, it appears that these documents were not adequately considered in the Tribunal's assessment.
18. In addition to the aforementioned documentary evidence, the claimants have presented the testimonies of witnesses P.Ws.1 to 3.
During the cross-examination of P.Ws.1 and 2, the respondents did not raise any questions regarding the charge sheet submitted by the police.
Furthermore, they - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB failed to provide any oral or documentary evidence to challenge the testimony provided by the claimants.

The Tribunal's assessment of the evidence lacks proper justification and reasoning, as it concluded that both the driver of the Bolero vehicle and the driver of the TATA APE equally contributed to the accident, apportioning the responsibility at 50% for each party.
However, this allocation of responsibility is not legally sustainable.

Upon thorough re-evaluation of the evidence on record, it is our firm belief that the claimants have successfully demonstrated that the accident was a result of the rash and negligent actions of the driver operating the vehicle with registration number MH-09/CM-9623.

Hence, we answer point.No.1 as affirmative.
19.

P.W.1 Yashawant Gosavi has deposed in his evidence as to the fracture, operation, medical expenses and also disability and he has produced the Wound Certificate as Ex.P.4, 31 medical bills as Ex.P.5, X-ray report as Ex.P.6, disability certificate at Ex.P.7., x-ray films at Ex.P.8.
22.

P.W.3 Dr.Satish Devgouda Patil, has deposed in his evidence as to the disability of the petitioner,
he has also deposed as to the certificate issued by him as per Ex.P.7.

In Ex.P.7, Doctor has opined that considering the clinical and radiological findings and after going through ALIMCO, in my opinion petitioner-Yashawant has got permanent physical - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB disability to the extent of 50% to the right lower limb, 35% to the left lower limb and 20% to the right upper limb.
But the Tribunal has not considered the disability only on the ground that P.W.3 is not a treated Doctor.
Age of the petitioner was 45 years at the time of accident.

Considering the age, occupation and nature of injuries shown in the Wound Certificate and Disability Certificate issued by P.W.3, we are of the considered view that, it is just and appropriate to assess the permanent disability of the petitioner-Yashawant at 35% to the whole body.
23. The petitioner has not produced any proof as to his income.

Therefore, considering the chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the Tribunal chose the notional income at Rs.8,000/- per month, then it comes to (Rs.8,000/- X 12 X 14 X 35/100) = Rs.4,70,400/-.

24. Considering the evidence adduced by the petitioner, it is just and proper to award the compensation on the following heads :
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 80,000/-
2 Loss of future earnings Rs.4,70,400/-

Accordingly, petitioner-Yashavant is entitled for enhancement of compensation.
26. With regard to quantum of compensation in MVC.No.700/2016 is concerned, the petitioner-Sachin Sakharam Gosavi examined himself as P.W.2.
He has deposed in his evidence that he was hale and healthy prior to the accident and aged 24 years.
Prior to this accident, he was doing scrap business and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further he has deposed about the injuries caused to him and also disability.

27. Apart from this oral and documentary evidence, he has produced Wound Certificate at Ex.P.9, 31 medical bills Ex.P.10, x-ray report Ex.P.11, Disability Certificate at Ex.P.12, four x-ray films at Ex.P.13.

He has also adduced the evidence of Dr.Satish Devgouda Patil, who has issued Ex.P.12.
- 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB 28.
P.W.3 also deposed as to the issuance of Ex.P.12 the Disability Certificate.

Considering the clinical and radiological findings and after going through ALIMCO, Doctor has opined that permanent physical disability amounting to 60% to left lower limb and 30% to the right lower limb.
29. The Tribunal's evaluation of the petitioner, Sachin's disability, was limited to 12%, and the notional income was determined to be Rs.7,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal's reasoning for arriving at this 12% disability assessment lacks proper elucidation.

Upon a thorough examination of the nature of the injuries sustained, the testimonies provided by P.W.2 and P.W.3, and the Disability Certificate, our considered opinion is that a more accurate reflection of the permanent disability should be at 30% encompassing the entire body of petitioner Sachin.
According to the guidelines outlined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the appropriate notional income for the petitioner should be Rs.8,000/- per month.
Consequently, the loss of future earnings for Sachin would be calculated as (Rs.8,000/- X 12 X 18 X 30/100) = Rs.5,18,400/-.

Accordingly, petitioner-Sachin is entitled for enhanced compensation.
Hence, we answer the point Nos.2 in partly affirmative.

32. Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
(i) Both appeals are allowed in part.

(ii) Petitioner-Yashawant (MFA.No.104276 of  2017) is entitled for enhanced  compensation of Rs.8,05,464/- and petitioner-Sachin (MFA No.104277 of 2017) is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,35,400/- with interest at the rate of - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB 6% per annum from the date of respective petitions till its realization.
(iii) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 in both claim petitions are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation awarded by this Court.
(iv) Insurance company in both appeals is directed to deposit the amount awarded within a period of 30 days from the date of award.
(v) Draw decree accordingly.

As a result, respondents 1 and 2, who respectively represent the vehicle's owner and its insurer, are considered liable to provide compensation for the resultant damages and losses experienced by the claimants.
5. In response to the service of notice, both respondents have appeared through their respective counsel and filed their separate objections by denying the contents of petitions and contended that the amount of compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and the alleged accident has occurred due to the fault of the driver of said TATA APE vehicle.
The owner and the insurer of TATA APE vehicle are necessary parties to the petitions.
Out of the compensation amount, the Tribunal has deducted 50% of the compensation on the ground that petitioners have not impleaded the insured and insurer of TATA APE vehicle.
However, the Tribunal has erred in not relying upon the evidence of P.W.3 on the ground that he is not a treated Doctor and considering the disability only to the extent of 12% for the purpose of awarding compensation.
The Tribunal ought to have considered the disability of the petitioner at 70%.
However, the Tribunal has erred in not relying the evidence of P.W.3 and has taken the disability at 12%.
The Tribunal ought to have considered the disability of the petitioner at 70%.
The Tribunal has also not awarded the just and proper compensation to the other heads as per the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Santosh Devi vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd and Other, reported in 2012 ACJ 1428.
opennyai_summary.issue:
After clubbing of both petitions, the Tribunal, based on the rival pleadings in both claim petitions,
has framed the common issues as under:
"(1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 09.11.2015 at about 07.15 hours within the limits of New Pargaon village near Asmita Daba, petitioner sustained injuries in the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the vehicle bearing registration no.MH-09/CM-9623 by its driver?
(2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
(3) What order?"
14. Having heard the arguments on both sides, the following points would arise for our consideration :
(1) Whether the Tribunal has committed an error in taking the award amount to the extent of 50% only on the ground that owner and insurer of the TATA APE motor vehicle is not impleaded in the claim petitions?
Shri Sachin S/O Sakharam Gosavi vs Shri. Balavant S/O Baburao Barge on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140503038/
5 (2) Whether the appellants in both appeals have made out a ground for enhancement of the compensation as sought for ?
(3) What order or award?
15. Our answers to the above points are as under :
Point No.1 in the affirmative.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The Doctor (P.W.3) has opined that petitioner has permanent physical disability to the extent of 60% to left lower limb and 30% to right lower limb.
As against this, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submit that the Tribunal has passed the impugned Judgment and Award in accordance with law and facts and there are no grounds to interfere with the same, accordingly sought for dismissal of the appeals.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the absence of charge sheet and rough sketch & in view the admission of PW 1, it can safely be said that petitioner Yashawant Laxman Gosavi was also at fault in causing the accident.
Considering the age, occupation and nature of injuries shown in the Wound Certificate and Disability Certificate issued by P.W.3, we are of the considered view that, it is just and appropriate to assess the permanent disability of the petitioner-Yashawant at 35% to the whole body.
23. The petitioner has not produced any proof as to his income.
29. The Tribunal's evaluation of the petitioner, Sachin's disability, was limited to 12%, and the notional income was determined to be Rs.7,000/- per month.
Upon a thorough examination of the nature of the injuries sustained, the testimonies provided by P.W.2 and P.W.3, and the Disability Certificate, our considered opinion is that a more accurate reflection of the permanent disability should be at 30% encompassing the entire body of petitioner Sachin.
opennyai_summary.decision:
According to the guidelines outlined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the appropriate notional income for the petitioner should be Rs.8,000/- per month.
Consequently, the loss of future earnings for Sachin would be calculated as (Rs.8,000/- X 12 X 18 X 30/100) = Rs.5,18,400/-.
Considering the nature of injuries, pain and agony and loss of future earnings, it is just and appropriate to award the compensation as under :
1
For pain and sufferings Rs. 80,000/-
2 Loss of future earnings Rs.5,18,400/- 3
For future medical expenses Rs. 20,000/- 4 Loss of income during laid up period Rs. 24,000/- 5
Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
6
For food, nourishment, Rs. 43,000/-
 transportation and attendant  charges
. 
 Total Rs.7,35,400/-
31.
Accordingly, petitioner-Sachin is entitled for enhanced compensation.
Hence, we answer the point Nos.2 in partly affirmative.
32. Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
(i) Both appeals are allowed in part.
(ii) Petitioner-Yashawant (MFA.No.104276 of  2017) is entitled for enhanced  compensation of Rs.8,05,464/- and petitioner-Sachin (MFA No.104277 of 2017) is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,35,400/- with interest at the rate of - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8953-DB 6% per annum from the date of respective petitions till its realization.
(iii) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 in both claim petitions are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation awarded by this Court.
(iv) Insurance company in both appeals is directed to deposit the amount awarded within a period of 30 days from the date of award.
(v) Draw decree accordingly.
